query: Which material can be used for ductility, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Titanium alloys with a specific microstructure, characterized by a high volume fraction of equiaxed alpha grains, will exhibit enhanced ductility due to the grain boundary-mediated plasticity mechanism.
generation.material_initial_state: Polycrystalline titanium alloy with a mixture of alpha and beta phases
generation.intervention: Thermomechanical processing to control microstructure, involving hot rolling and recrystallization annealing at 900°C for 2 hours
generation.conditions: Room temperature and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1
generation.mechanism: Grain boundary-mediated plasticity, where grain boundaries act as sinks for dislocations, reducing the stress concentration and promoting ductile deformation
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in elongation to failure by 25% compared to the baseline, with a baseline elongation to failure of 15%
generation.baseline: Conventional titanium alloy with a lamellar microstructure
generation.uncertainty: The actual ductility enhancement may vary depending on the specific alloy composition and processing conditions, and the grain boundary-mediated plasticity mechanism may not be the only contributing factor

falsification_experiment.design: Uniaxial tensile testing of titanium alloy samples with controlled microstructure
measurements: Microstructure characterization using electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured elongation to failure is less than 18.75%, the hypothesis is falsified
